title: The Impact of Media Use on the Mental Health and Time Perspective of Adolescents
summary:
This study examines how extensively adolescents use digital media and whether this is related to their mental health. This includes, for example, depressive mood, anxiety, attention problems, or stress reactions after difficult experiences. The study also looks at how adolescents think about their past, present, and future, and whether this personal “time perspective” influences how they use media or how they feel emotionally.

The adolescents complete digital questionnaires. Participation is voluntary, and all data are collected in a pseudonymized form. The aim of the study is to better understand the role that media use plays in the mental health of young people and to identify factors that may protect them.

interventions.name: Clinical sample: Patients receiving outpatient child and adolescent psychiatric treatment complete digital questionnaires assessing the type and extent of media use, resilience, time perspectives, and psychopathology (borderline symptoms, ADHD, depression, anxiety, PTSD symptoms).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Age between 14 and 20 years
• Outpatient child and adolescent psychiatric treatment at the Wuppertal outpatient clinic of the Center for Mental Health in Childhood and Adolescence at Sana‑Klinikum Remscheid (study site)
• Average intellectual functioning based on clinical judgment
• Sufficient German language skills to complete the questionnaires
Exclusion criteria:
• Intellectual disability
• Psychotic symptoms
• Illiteracy
• Age below 14 years
• Completion of the 21st year of life
